caption: The drawing consists of technical line illustrations in black ink on a tan or beige background, depicting a bed from two perspectives: a frontal view labeled "DRAWN FROM FOOT OF BED" on the left and a "SIDE ELEVATION" on the right. The bed frame, which is composed of turned and rectangular sections, includes detailed renderings of the headboard, footboard, legs, and decorative top rails. There is a curved line above the bed in the side elevation, likely representing a canopy or a frame for a mosquito net or drapes. Underneath the main bed frame, there is a rectangular trundle bed marked "TRUNDLE" that fits beneath the main structure. Measurement annotations are present, including vertical dimensions such as "82 3/4" and horizontal distances such as "40" and "65". Various segments of the bedposts are labeled with their lengths, and dotted lines indicate their alignment between views. The text notes that the piece is a "BED—CHERRY—MAPLE with TRUNDLE BED—ROPE SPRING (TRUNDLE MOVABLE) CIRCA 1800," and provides a scale of "1 1/2" = 1'." The drawing is credited to "JACK BOCHNER BKLYN MUSEUM" and references the "SCHENCK HOUSE—CANARSIE PARK, L.I. BUILT BEFORE 1773."
title: Bed and Trundle Bed
